title.value: CrossSplit: Mitigating Label Noise Memorization through Data Splitting
title.justification: The title was explicitly stated multiple times throughout the document, and it accurately reflects the main focus of the research, which is about the CrossSplit method for mitigating label noise memorization.
title.quote: CrossSplit: Mitigating Label Noise Memorization through Data Splitting

extractions.description: This paper introduces CrossSplit, a novel method for robust training of deep learning models in the presence of noisy labels. CrossSplit uses a pair of neural networks trained on disjoint parts of a labeled dataset, implementing cross-split label correction through peer predictions and cross-split semi-supervised learning. The method seeks to prevent memorization of noisy labels, outperforming existing approaches across several datasets, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and mini-WebVision, by leveraging data splitting, label correction, and class-balancing normalization.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is on improving the robustness of deep learning models against noisy labels in datasets, which is a computer science and machine learning problem. The paper does not focus on climate or ecological sustainable development issues or applications.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We approach the problem of improving robustness of deep learning algorithms in the presence of label noise.

primary_category.quote: This problem has been addressed in various ways in the recent literature. Two common approaches are label correction and sample selection.

secondary_categories.quote: The goal of this paper is to propose a novel robust training scheme that addresses some of these drawbacks.
